creator.voiceNotes: {"style": "warm, personal, thoughtful", "tone": "honest and direct without being preachy", "avoid": "generic recommendations or forcing positivity"}

shelfItems.title: Falling - Harry Styles
shelfItems.description: A vulnerable ballad from Fine Line
shelfItems.creatorNote: The piano version gets me every time. Perfect for when you need to sit with your feelings instead of running from them.

shelfItems.title: Motion Sickness - Phoebe Bridgers
shelfItems.description: Indie folk from Stranger in the Alps
shelfItems.creatorNote: This got me through my first real heartbreak. 'I have emotional motion sickness' — sometimes you just need someone to name exactly how you feel.

shelfItems.title: First Day of My Life - Bright Eyes
shelfItems.description: Folk song from I'm Wide Awake, It's Morning
shelfItems.creatorNote: Conor's voice cracks and it's perfect. This is what hope sounds like when you've been down for a while.

shelfItems.title: Amado Mio - Pink Martini
shelfItems.description: Latin jazz standard
shelfItems.creatorNote: Pure romance in a song. I play this when I'm cooking dinner and want to feel like I'm in a film.

shelfItems.title: Peaceful Piano
shelfItems.description: Spotify's official peaceful piano playlist
shelfItems.creatorNote: This is my writing playlist. No lyrics to distract you, just beautiful piano that keeps you in flow.

shelfItems.title: sad girl starter pack
shelfItems.description: For when you need to feel your feelings
shelfItems.creatorNote: Not actually just for sad girls — for anyone who needs to cry it out. Sometimes that's exactly what you need.

shelfItems.title: Million Dollar Baby
shelfItems.description: 2004 drama directed by Clint Eastwood
shelfItems.creatorNote: This wrecked me. It's about boxing but it's really about found family and the choices we make for the people we love. Bring tissues.

shelfItems.title: The Lives of Others
shelfItems.description: 2006 German drama about surveillance in East Berlin
shelfItems.creatorNote: One of the most beautiful films about empathy I've ever seen. Shows how art can change someone, even in the darkest times.

shelfItems.title: Heat
shelfItems.description: 1995 crime drama with Pacino and De Niro
shelfItems.creatorNote: That coffee shop scene changed how I think about character scenes. Two people talking shouldn't be this tense, but it is.

shelfItems.title: The War of Art - Steven Pressfield
shelfItems.description: A book about overcoming creative resistance
shelfItems.creatorNote: Read this when you're avoiding your creative work. It's blunt and sometimes harsh, but it's the kick I needed to stop making excuses.

shelfItems.title: Giovanni's Room - James Baldwin
shelfItems.description: A novel about love and self-deception
shelfItems.creatorNote: Baldwin writes about longing and regret in a way that feels timeless. Every sentence is perfect. Read it slowly.

shelfItems.title: The Song of Achilles - Madeline Miller
shelfItems.description: A retelling of the Iliad from Patroclus's perspective
shelfItems.creatorNote: If you think you don't like Greek mythology, try this. It made me cry on the train. Just pure, devastating love.

shelfItems.title: Daisy Jones & The Six - Taylor Jenkins Reid
shelfItems.description: A novel about a 1970s rock band told as an oral history
shelfItems.creatorNote: The oral history format makes it fly by. It's fiction but feels so real — captures what it's like to make art with people you love and hate.

shelfItems.title: Structure - The New Yorker
shelfItems.description: John McPhee on writing structure
shelfItems.creatorNote: McPhee breaks down exactly how he structures his pieces. Transformed how I think about organizing my own writing. So practical.

shelfItems.title: Joni Mitchell on Blue - The Guardian
shelfItems.description: Joni Mitchell reflects on her landmark album
shelfItems.creatorNote: She talks about writing from a place of total vulnerability. It's brave and it's why Blue still matters. Required reading for songwriters.

shelfItems.title: Phoebe Bridgers Is Not Your Sad Girl
shelfItems.description: New Yorker interview with Phoebe Bridgers
shelfItems.creatorNote: She's hilarious and smart about the 'sad girl' label. Also talks about community in music — not as competition but as support.

shelfItems.title: Time Out Market Lisboa
shelfItems.description: Food hall in Cais do Sodré, Lisbon
shelfItems.creatorNote: Best place to eat in Lisbon if you want to try lots of things. Go for lunch, get the pastel de nata afterward, thank me later.

shelfItems.title: Barbican Centre - London
shelfItems.description: Arts and learning centre in the City of London
shelfItems.creatorNote: The architecture is stunning and it's never pretentious. I go to the library to write and catch whatever's on in the cinema.

shelfItems.title: Stanfords Travel Bookshop - London
shelfItems.description: The world's largest travel bookshop
shelfItems.creatorNote: I can lose hours here. Even if you're not planning a trip, it makes you want to go somewhere. The old maps section is magic.

shelfItems.title: Miradouro de Santa Catarina - Lisbon
shelfItems.description: Viewpoint in Bairro Alto overlooking the Tagus
shelfItems.creatorNote: Best sunset spot in Lisbon. Grab a beer from the kiosk, sit on the wall, and watch the light change. Locals still go, which says everything.

shelfItems.quoteText: You can't wait for inspiration. You have to go after it with a club.
shelfItems.title: Jack London on Creativity
shelfItems.creatorNote: I have this on my wall. Some days you don't feel like creating, and that's exactly when you need to show up anyway.

shelfItems.quoteText: The cure for anything is salt water: sweat, tears, or the sea.
shelfItems.title: Isak Dinesen
shelfItems.creatorNote: When I'm stuck in my head, I remember this. Go for a run, let yourself cry, or find water. It always helps.

shelfItems.quoteText: We must be willing to let go of the life we planned so as to have the life that is waiting for us.
shelfItems.title: Joseph Campbell
shelfItems.creatorNote: I read this after a big breakup and it shifted something. Sometimes the best thing isn't what you thought you wanted.

shelfItems.quoteText: There is no greater agony than bearing an untold story inside you.
shelfItems.title: Maya Angelou
shelfItems.creatorNote: This is why I write. Your story matters, even if it feels small. Especially if it feels small.

shelfItems.title: Music Theory for Beginners
shelfItems.description: Free online music theory course
shelfItems.creatorNote: This taught me enough theory to write better melodies. You don't need to know everything, just enough to unlock new ideas.

shelfItems.title: The Marginalian (Brain Pickings)
shelfItems.description: Maria Popova's weekly newsletter on culture, art, and philosophy
shelfItems.creatorNote: Maria finds connections between art, science, and life that I'd never see. Her weekly emails are long but worth it.

shelfItems.title: Lua - Bright Eyes
shelfItems.description: Folk song from I'm Wide Awake, It's Morning
shelfItems.creatorNote: The live version from the Roisin Dubh is the one. It's messy and emotional and perfect for 2am feelings.

shelfItems.title: Que Sera Sera - Pink Martini
shelfItems.description: Vintage standard
shelfItems.creatorNote: My mom used to sing this. It's a good reminder when you're anxious about the future — whatever will be, will be.

shelfItems.title: Finding Nemo
shelfItems.description: 2003 Pixar animated film
shelfItems.creatorNote: Don't let anyone tell you it's just a kids' film. 'Just keep swimming' got me through some dark times. Cry every time.

shelfItems.title: The Crossroads of Should and Must - Elle Luna
shelfItems.description: A short book about choosing your must
shelfItems.creatorNote: You can read this in an hour and it'll make you think for weeks. Should is safe, must is scary. Pick must.

shelfItems.title: How to Read More - Austin Kleon
shelfItems.description: Practical tips on reading more books
shelfItems.creatorNote: His advice is so simple it's almost annoying. Carry a book, quit books you don't like, read before bed. But it works.

messages.text: Hey! Just wanted to say your last track was beautiful. The quieter moments really got me.
Thank you so much Sam! Those quieter songs are actually my favorites from the album too 💙
I've been listening to it on repeat when I need to just... think, you know? Really hits different late at night.
Do you have any other song recommendations? I love that vulnerable, stripped-back vibe.
Hi Maya! I'm traveling to Lisbon next month and I remember you mentioned you love it there. Any recommendations?
Oh amazing! You're going to love it. Let me think about some spots for you.
Thanks!! I'm really into food and just wandering around, not so much touristy stuff.
Also if you know any good fado places? I've never heard it live.
Your music has been helping me through a rough breakup. Thank you for being so honest in your songs.
I'm so sorry you're going through that. Sending you lots of love 💛
It's been hard. We were together for 3 years. I keep thinking about all the plans we made.
Sorry for being heavy. I just don't know who else to talk to about this stuff.
Don't apologize. Breakups are the worst. Be gentle with yourself okay? 💙
Thank you. That means a lot. Do you have any songs or anything that helped you when you went through this?
I've been trying to write songs but I have no idea what I'm doing lol. How did you get started?
Honestly just by doing it badly for a long time! 😂 But it's the best feeling when something clicks.
That's encouraging haha. I have all these feelings but no idea how to turn them into actual songs.
Did you learn music theory or just figure it out by ear?
Bit of both! I learned enough theory to unlock new ideas, but the feeling always comes first.
Your newsletter this week about finding your voice hit so hard. I've been struggling with that in my own creative work.
Thank you for reading! It's such a journey, isn't it?
Yeah. I keep feeling like I need to sound like someone else to be taken seriously.
But then I read your stuff and it's so YOU, you know? That's what makes it good.
Weird question but do you have any book recommendations? Your taste is immaculate.
Not weird at all! I love talking books. What kind of thing are you in the mood for?
Something beautiful but also heartbreaking? I'm in that kind of mood lately.
That Phoebe Bridgers song you posted about changed my life. I can't stop listening to Motion Sickness.
RIGHT?! That whole album is perfect.
Do you have more sad indie recs? I'm going through something and this is exactly what I need.
Just discovered your music through a playlist. Obsessed. How long have you been making music?
Thank you! About 6 years seriously, but I've been writing since I was a teenager.
That's so cool. Your lyrics feel really personal but also like they could be about anyone.
I need something uplifting today. Everything feels heavy. Any recommendations?
Sending you good vibes! Let me think what might help...
Thank you 💛 Just need something to remind me things will be okay.
Your writing about creativity really resonates with me. Do you have any advice for staying consistent?
It's so hard! I try to show up even when I don't feel inspired. Discipline over motivation.
That makes sense. I always wait to feel inspired and then nothing happens lol.
Do you have any resources that helped you with that mindset shift?
